Former Rehoboth Beach Mayor Stan Mills was recognized for his nearly two decades of service to Rehoboth Beach with a celebration at the city’s convention center Sept. 23.
The two-hour-long event was highlighted by a brief round of local organizations recalling the hard work Mills did over the years. His accomplishments range from the obvious – rebuilding the Boardwalk and overseeing the construction of the new beach patrol headquarters – to the less obvious – hundreds of medallions on storm drains reminding people the water drains into the city's lakes and the painting of rainbow crosswalks on Baltimore Avenue.
City Manager Taylour Tedder declared Sept. 23 as Stan Mills Day in Rehoboth Beach. Mills was presented with tributes from the House and the Senate by Rep. Claire Snyder-Hall, D-Lewes. Commissioner Patrick Gossett, who worked alongside Mills for 13 years, spoke on behalf of city commissioners. Representing local organizations were Rehoboth Beach Homeowners Association President Susan Gay, Rehoboth Beach-Dewey Beach Chamber of Commerce President Kate VanVorst, Rehoboth Beach Main Street President Suzie Martin and CAMP Rehoboth Executive Director Robin Brennan.
Mills took the floor when acknowledgements of his service were complete. He took the opportunity to encourage everyone in the room to volunteer with any of the worthy local causes or to donate to those causes. Become involved with something, anything, said Mills.
Mills was mayor for six years. His last day was Sept. 18. Prior to being mayor, he was a commissioner for 12 years before deciding not to seek re-election in 2019. He was also on committees and task forces before becoming a commissioner.
Mills isn’t exactly done helping the city. He remains chair of the city’s Boardwalk historic designation task force and, he said, he looks forward to continuing to volunteer at events.
